batch_strategy: Freeze the 32 distinct candidate IDs below and their supplied premeasurement predictions together. Combine scaffold-specific solvent-response experiments, controlled loading contrasts, and limited diagnostics of unusual labels. Measured evidence IDs appear only in the hypotheses' typed observed-ID lists.

choices.reason: Measure m106 at 2/1 and 100 ul. Recent measurements at 10/1 and 20/1 substantially exceeded their acquisition predictions. This lower-ratio anchor locates the beginning of its steep ether-ketone response.
Measure m127 at 20/1 and 150 ul. At 50 ul, measured retention decreases between 20/1 and 50/1. Paired with the selected 50/1 condition, this tests whether that local maximum transfers across loading.

Measure m127 at 50/1 and 150 ul, completing the selected fixed-loading pair. Its measured 50-ul response was only 11.65/23.65 mL, far earlier than the acquisition prediction. This tests whether the compact weak-eluent response recurs at higher loading.

Measure m13 at 10/1 and 100 ul. Existing 50- and 150-ul measurements differ substantially in onset, about 53 versus 37 mL, while both finish near 94 mL. The intermediate loading tests endpoint-specific interpolation rather than a shared loading shift.

Measure m92 at 1/1 with a 50-ul sample and a 200-ul EA loading plug. This establishes the strong-eluent reference for the selected loading-solvent comparison and extends its measured alpha-ketoester response curve.

Measure m92 at the same ratio, density, sample volume, and plug volume as the selected EA-loaded experiment, changing loading solvent to PE. The model predicts a modest difference; the controlled pair tests whether that condition feature captures a transferable loading-solvent interaction.

Measure alkynediester m91 at 50/1 and 150 ul. Its measured 5/1 response is compact, and the model predicts a compact weak-eluent finish despite very high CW distance. This tests transfer between distinct multi-ester environments.

Measure phenylmalonate m75 at 20/1 and 50 ul. Its measured 1/1 condition at this loading is compact. Together with selected 50/1, this anchors the predicted transition and distinguishes its response from bromomalonate and beta-ketoesters.

Measure m75 at 50/1 and 50 ul, matched to selected 20/1. Bromomalonate grows substantially in weak eluent, whereas unsubstituted malonate remains compact. This pair tests whether phenyl substitution produces the predicted retention growth.

Measure ethyl acetoacetate m82 at 5/1 and 150 ul. Measured 2/1 at this loading finishes near 20 mL, while 10/1 at 100 ul finishes near 46 mL. This locates finish expansion while testing loading transfer.

Measure methyl acetoacetate m95 at 5/1 and 50 ul, between measured 2/1 and 20/1 conditions at the same loading. This complements m82 and tests response curvature across methyl and ethyl beta-ketoesters, acknowledging their different loading-plug volumes.

Measure tert-butyl beta-ketoester m25 at 50/1 and 150 ul. Its measured 10/1 condition at 100 ul leaves the predicted weak-eluent growth poorly anchored. This extends beta-ketoester coverage across a sterically distinct ester substituent.

Measure trimethoxybenzene m110 at 5/1 and 50 ul. Its predicted finish of 19.38 mL exceeds the measured 10/1 finish of 14.30 mL at identical loading. This directly tests a possible interpolation artifact in an ether-only aromatic scaffold.

Measure m110 at 50/1 and 50 ul, extending the selected 5/1 and measured 10/1 comparison. A measured 50/1 reference exists at 150 ul. This tests loading transfer at the weak-eluent endpoint while constraining the broader response shape.

Measure m117 at 10/1 and 50 ul. The 100-ul label has a late onset and slightly reversed endpoints, which the current prediction largely transfers to 50 ul. This tests whether the unusual onset regime recurs at another loading.

Measure m73 at 2/1 and 50 ul, immediately beyond its newly measured late 1/1 condition. Late or reversed endpoints have now recurred at several low-ratio conditions. This tests where that regime changes without assigning its cause to loading alone.

Measure p-xylene m133 at 2/1 and 100 ul. Its measured 50-ul condition is unusually late and narrow, while 20/1 at 100 ul is much earlier. This tests recurrence of a localized response that conflicts with a simple nonpolar-compound prior.

Measure hindered tertiary alcohol m203 at 10/1 and 150 ul. Existing 1/1 and 5/1 observations are relatively compact. The selected 20/1 partner tests the predicted steep response in a sparsely anchored alcohol environment.

Measure m203 at 20/1 and 150 ul, matched to selected 10/1. The model predicts growth from approximately 21/37 to 48/84 mL, with very high CW distance. This pair tests the solvent sensitivity of its hindered tertiary-alcohol environment.

Measure dibenzylamine m212 at 10/1 and 150 ul. Its fixed-loading measured response rises from about 6/17 at 2/1 to 23/40 mL at 5/1. This tests continued growth for a secondary amine in a high-CW-distance condition.

Measure biphenyl ketone m68 at 50/1 and 100 ul, extending measured 20/1 at about 6/18 mL. Its high CW distance and moderate predicted response test transfer between lipophilic aryl ketones with differing weak-eluent behavior.

Measure conjugated ketone m164 at 50/1 and 100 ul. Its measured 5/1 condition is compact, and related chalcone has a moderately expanded 50/1 interval. This tests predicted finish expansion with relatively limited onset growth.

Measure ortho-fluorobenzonitrile m163 at 50/1 and 50 ul. Its measured 5/1 anchor is about 10/17 mL. This tests the unmeasured weak-eluent region and transfer from the retained ortho-bromobenzonitrile response.

Measure salicylaldehyde m197 at 50/1 and 50 ul, beyond measured 20/1 at about 11/35 mL. This tests the predicted finish increase in a phenol-aldehyde environment; intramolecular hydrogen bonding is a possible chemical explanation, not an established finding.

Measure m81 at 2/1 and 150 ul. Higher-loading finishes were short at both 5/1 and 10/1, while lower-loading 2/1 measurements finish near 12 mL. This tests whether that loading association begins before the disputed higher-ratio region.

Measure m81 at 50/1 and 100 ul. The 50-ul reference finishes near 17 mL, and identical-input 100-ul measurements at 20/1 disagree. This constrains the weak-eluent continuation without assuming a universal loading-driven finish reduction.
Measure sulfur-aldehyde m129 at 20/1 and 100 ul, between measured 10/1 at about 10/24 and 50/1 at 38/63 mL. This locates its transition after repeated historical overprediction at lower ratios.

Measure tertiary alcohol m51 at 5/1 and 100 ul. Its measured 1/1 condition is about 7/12 mL, while the model predicts 28/36 mL at 5/1. This tests an uncovered transition and complements the structurally different tertiary alcohol m203.

Measure para-cyanoacetophenone m31 at 10/1 and 50 ul, extending measured 5/1 at about 13/32 mL. Cyano-benzophenone is much more compact at 10/1 and the same sample volume. This tests transfer across carbonyl–nitrile structural environments.

Measure para-fluoroacetophenone m34 at 20/1 and 50 ul. Measured 10/1 at this loading is about 11/22 mL, whereas the model predicts little onset growth at 20/1. This tests intermediate-ratio transfer after the proposed Br/I finish crossover failed.

Measure bromobenzyl alcohol m207 at 2/1 and 100 ul, matched in ratio to the recent 150-ul measurement. At 5/1, the 100-ul label is much more compact than both 50- and 150-ul labels. This tests whether that anomaly is ratio-localized.

Measure fused ether-aldehyde m194 at 1/1 and 150 ul. Existing 50- and 100-ul labels have similar onset but finishes near 10 and 36 mL. This missing loading level discriminates finish-specific loading associations from unexplained variation.

hypotheses.content: Weak-eluent response is strongly scaffold-dependent. Some ether-carbonyl, beta-ketoester, alcohol, and basic scaffolds show steep onset or finish growth, while other acceptor-containing compounds remain compact. Functional-group counts alone do not support a shared late-retention correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Contrasting growing and compact responses can teach graph-condition interactions and limit inappropriate transfer of large retention corrections across chemically different rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which unanchored weak-eluent curves grow steeply or plateau across malonates, beta-ketoesters, hindered alcohols, nitriles, and lipophilic ketones?

hypotheses.content: Recorded loading conditions can associate differently with onset and finish, and these relationships depend on scaffold and solvent ratio. Sample volume and density-times-volume amount are coupled. Loading-plug effects and unexplained label variation remain relevant; a single monotonic loading law is unsupported.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controlled contrasts can reveal associations that nearly invariant loading predictions miss while preventing isolated inconsistent labels from becoming general loading rules.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do the m81 and m207 loading associations extend to 2/1, does m13 interpolate differently for its two endpoints, and does changing only m92 loading solvent alter retention?

hypotheses.content: Finish behavior requires endpoint-specific calibration. Similar onset can coexist with substantial finish differences across loading or structure, including in strong-eluent conditions. Some variation may remain unexplained by the supplied inputs.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Joint endpoint labels can repair finish predictions without forcing an equivalent onset shift, improving accuracy across compact and expanded elution intervals.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: At m194 1/1 and 150 ul, does the finish resemble the compact 50-ul result, the extended 100-ul result, or an intermediate response?

hypotheses.content: Sulfoxide, aryl thioether-ketone, and aryl thioether-aldehyde responses differ substantially. Measurement rejected the predicted m199 5/1-to-10/1 plateau; m129 remains substantially more compact at 10/1. Sulfur-family corrections should remain sensitive to functional environment and solvent ratio.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: This prevents the large sulfoxide correction from propagating indiscriminately to sulfide-containing carbonyl compounds and helps locate their distinct solvent-response transitions.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: How far has m129 progressed toward its measured 50/1 response by 20/1 at fixed loading?

hypotheses.content: Substitution-specific response curvature remains important, but predicted nonmonotonicity needs direct testing. The Br/I finish crossover at 20/1 was not observed. At 50 ul, m127 instead shows a measured decrease from 20/1 to 50/1; transfer across loading is unresolved. The predicted m110 finish decrease from 5/1 to measured 10/1 is also untested.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched response experiments distinguish reproducible graph-solvent interactions from interpolation artifacts and influential isolated labels.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does m127 retain its 20/1 maximum at 150 ul, and do new fixed-loading m110 measurements support the predicted response shape around its measured 10/1 condition?

hypotheses.content: Unusual late or narrow elution regimes cannot simply be dismissed as isolated observations, but their causes are unresolved. m73 now has several reversed-endpoint records, and identical-input m81 labels differ substantially. Measurement variation or absent metadata remain possibilities rather than established explanations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Limited adjacent-condition diagnostics can constrain what is predictable from the recorded features and reduce spurious solvent or loading relationships inferred from anomalous rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m73 late regime persist at 2/1, does the m117 10/1 onset spike recur at 50 ul, and does m133 reproduce its late 2/1 behavior at 100 ul?

feedback_interpretation:
The latest measurements reject two specific model-derived proposals. At 20/1, m30 still finishes later than m35 despite nearly coincident onsets, so the proposed Br/I finish crossover failed. At fixed 150-ul loading, m199 rises from 27.42/52.38 mL at 5/1 to 57.86/114.60 mL at 10/1, rejecting the predicted plateau. Conversely, m127 at 50/1 was much earlier than its acquisition prediction and earlier than its measured 20/1 condition. This motivates testing that local maximum at another loading rather than imposing monotonic growth.

The m106 pair and m78 finish strengthen evidence for steep, scaffold-specific weak-eluent responses. Compact m8, more moderate m87, and repeated m129 overpredictions strengthen the need to prevent broad transfer of late-retention corrections. The recent m128 loading result and m36 1/1 result were comparatively well predicted, reducing the urgency of nearby measurements.

Loading feedback is endpoint-specific. At 150 ul, m13 onset is lower than at 50 ul at both 5/1 and 10/1, while finish is similar or later. The short m81 high-loading finish recurs at 5/1 and 10/1, but conflicting identical-input 20/1 labels limit a deterministic explanation. For m207, the 150-ul 5/1 finish resembles the 50-ul result much more than the compact 100-ul result, weakening a monotonic loading interpretation. New m73 reversed endpoints show that its unusual regime is recurrent; the ordinary m195 20/1 result at 50 ul weakens a loading-independent onset-peak interpretation. These errors are historical acquisition-time errors, not current-model residuals.
batch_rationale:
The batch resolves competing response models while extending coverage of unmeasured conditions. The m127 pair tests reproducibility of a measured local maximum; m110 tests a predicted intermediate dip and weak-eluent loading transfer. The m75 and m203 pairs test response curvature. The m92 pair changes only loading solvent, providing a controlled test of a recorded condition feature. m13, m81, m207, and m194 address endpoint-specific loading associations using measured neighboring conditions.

Exploration includes compact predicted multi-esters, moderately retained lipophilic ketones and nitriles, and growing alcohol and amine responses. Their learning value comes from unresolved structure-condition relationships, supported in several cases by high CW distance. The m73, m117, and m133 diagnostics receive limited batch space because unexplained variation may restrict their transferable information.

These labels may improve Row-distribution accuracy by teaching where response transitions occur, when structural analogies transfer, and when onset and finish need different corrections. Sample amount is the supplied density-times-volume feature; its independent effect cannot be separated from sample volume in these loading contrasts. Quantile spreads and CW distance remain secondary diagnostics: single-predictor quantiles are not calibrated epistemic uncertainty, and quantile crossing further limits their interpretation.
